port_page.name: Fishing Port
port_page.hero_subtitle: Working harbour of blue fishing boats, nets and morning catch — the living Atlantic face of El Jadida.
port_page.overview.title: Blue boats and daily catch
port_page.overview.p1: El Jadida’s fishing port is still a place of work: painted blue boats, nets drying, and the rhythm of boats leaving and returning. It is one of the most photogenic and honest corners of the town.
port_page.overview.p2: Come in the morning for activity. Stay out of restricted dock zones and ask before close-up photos of people at work. Grilled fish nearby is the natural follow-up.
port_page.overview.p3: The port sits close to the old town, so it fits easily between the cistern circuit and a medina afternoon.

port_page.faq.title: Fishing Port FAQ
port_page.faq.q1.question: Can I walk around freely?
port_page.faq.q1.answer: Public edges yes; respect barriers and working crews.
port_page.faq.q2.question: Best time?
port_page.faq.q2.answer: Morning when boats and markets are most active.
port_page.faq.q3.question: Where to eat the catch?
port_page.faq.q3.answer: Simple grilled-fish places cluster near the harbour.
port_page.faq.q4.question: Good for photos?
port_page.faq.q4.answer: Yes — blue hulls and harbour light are the classic El Jadida shots.
port_page.faq.q5.question: Safe with children?
port_page.faq.q5.answer: Yes on the public promenade; hold hands near the water edge.
